Predict tree height: choose best available DBH–height model or run all candidates

Source: R/hd.R
hd.Rd

hd() is a convenience wrapper that predicts total tree height (m) from DBH by selecting, per tree, one (or more) of the DBH–height (hd_*()) models listed in hd_model_registry(). It is the DBH–height counterpart of vol().

Usage

hd(
  DBH,
  species,
  jurisdiction,
  ...,
  bec_zone = NA_character_,
  bc_region = NA_character_,
  stand_origin = "natural",
  pick_best = TRUE,
  keep_model_id = TRUE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Diameter at breast height (cm).

species

Character vector. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.MAR").

jurisdiction

Character vector. Province/territory code (e.g. "ON").

...

Named predictors, using the hd_*() argument names (e.g. BA, HDOM, TPH, natural_subregion, ecoregion). Each must have length 1 or length(DBH); NA marks the predictor as unavailable for that tree. See hd_model_registry() for the predictors each model uses.

bec_zone

Optional character vector. BC biogeoclimatic zone code (e.g. "CWH", "IDF"), used to infer bc_region: CWH, CDF, MH and CMA are coastal; BG, BWBS, ESSF, ICH, IDF, IMA, MS, PP, SBPS, SBS, SWB and BAFA are interior. Ignored outside BC.

bc_region

Optional character vector, "coastal" or "interior". Alternative to bec_zone; if both are given they must agree. Ignored outside BC.

stand_origin

Character vector, "natural" (default) or "plantation". NA is treated as "natural".

pick_best

Logical. If TRUE (default), use the single best model per tree. If FALSE, run all eligible models and return a list (one tibble per tree), suitable as a list-column.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE (default), include a model_id column with the registry model ID used.

Value

If pick_best = TRUE, a tibble with one row per tree and column height (m), plus model_id if requested. Trees for which no model is eligible or succeeds get NA (with a warning). Warnings are also issued when a plantation tree uses a natural-stand model, or when a coastal- or interior-only BC model is used without bec_zone/bc_region.

If pick_best = FALSE, a list with one tibble per tree containing the outputs of every successful candidate model (height, and optionally model_id), ordered from most to least preferred.

Model selection logic

Selection is registry-driven and occurs per input tree:

  1. Geographic applicability: the model's province_scope must include jurisdiction.

  2. Species coverage: the model must have coefficients for species (exact match; no genus-level fallback).

  3. Stand origin: plantation-only models are used only when stand_origin = "plantation". For plantation trees, models fitted to plantations (or to both origins) are preferred; natural-stand models are used only as a fallback, with a warning.

  4. British Columbia coast vs interior: models fitted to coastal or interior BC only (see bc_region in hd_model_registry()) are restricted to trees in that region when bec_zone or bc_region is given. When neither is given, they remain eligible and a warning is issued if one is used.

  5. Required predictors: every required predictor of the model (see get_hd_model_info()) must be supplied in ... and non-missing for the tree. Optional predictors (e.g. a region code) are passed on when non-missing.

  6. Ranking: among eligible models the highest rank is used. If the model fails for a tree (e.g. a species-specific predictor is missing, or a region code is not recognised), the next-ranked model is tried.

Important limitations and recommended use

  • Predictor definitions differ between sources. For example, basal area (BA) may be all-species or species-specific and computed with different minimum DBH thresholds; dominant height (HDOM) is defined differently by each source. hd() passes the same value to every model, so check the definitions with get_hd_model_info() before supplying stand-level predictors.

  • The ranking is a pragmatic default (more stand information, newer and more local models are preferred). If you require a specific model, call the hd_*() function directly.

  • Run with pick_best = FALSE during exploratory analyses to inspect which models are eligible and how sensitive results are to model choice.

  • Models' out-of-range warnings are passed through unchanged; their informational messages (e.g. which internal variant was used) are suppressed, since model_id reports the model used.

See also

hd_model_registry(), find_hd_models(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

## DBH only: best available DBH-only model
hd(DBH = c(12, 25), species = "PICE.MAR", jurisdiction = c("ON", "AB"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   height model_id           
#>    <dbl> <chr>              
#> 1   10.9 sharmazhang2004_eq5
#> 2   19.2 huang2016          

## Stand predictors unlock stand-level models where available
hd(
  DBH = 20, species = "PICE.MAR", jurisdiction = "ON",
  HDOM = 18, BA = 25, TPH = 1200
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   height model_id          
#>    <dbl> <chr>             
#> 1   16.5 sharma2016_natural

## BC: the BEC zone (or bc_region) selects coastal vs interior models
hd(DBH = c(30, 30), species = "PSEU.MEN", jurisdiction = "BC", bec_zone = c("CWH", "IDF"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   height model_id                
#>    <dbl> <chr>                   
#> 1   22.7 staudhammerlemay2000_dbh
#> 2   22.0 temesgen2004_m2         

## Compare all eligible models
hd(
  DBH = 20, species = "PICE.MAR", jurisdiction = "ON",
  HDOM = 18, BA = 25, TPH = 1200, pick_best = FALSE
)[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   height model_id           
#>    <dbl> <chr>              
#> 1   16.5 sharma2016_natural 
#> 2   16.5 sharmaparton2007   
#> 3   20.4 sharmazhang2004_eq2
#> 4   16.1 sharmazhang2004_eq5

## Inside dplyr::mutate()
trees <- tibble::tibble(
  DBH = c(15, 22, 30),
  species = c("PINU.BAN", "PICE.GLA", "PICE.MAR"),
  jurisdiction = c("ON", "AB", "AB"),
  natural_subregion = c(NA, "CM", "LF")
)
trees |>
  dplyr::mutate(hd(DBH, species, jurisdiction,
    natural_subregion = natural_subregion
  ))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>     DBH species  jurisdiction natural_subregion height model_id         
#>   <dbl> <chr>    <chr>        <chr>              <dbl> <chr>            
#> 1    15 PINU.BAN ON           NA                  14.5 zhang2002_overall
#> 2    22 PICE.GLA AB           CM                  21.3 huang2016        
#> 3    30 PICE.MAR AB           LF                  21.1 huang2016
